A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SDForger and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Retained content can be reliably matched across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original similarity benchmarks, downstream forecasting experiments, component ablations, runtime measurements and text-conditioned generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original analyses of retained variance, filtering failures and embedding dimensionality in downstream forecasting.

M1.justification: Segmentation, ICA/FPC embeddings, shuffled textual encoding, LLM generation, filtering and decoding remain unchanged. New filtering examples explain existing checks; nonlinear embeddings and parameter-efficient fine-tuning are proposed as future work.

E1.justification: The datasets and multisample, univariate, multivariate and text-conditioned tasks are retained. New stationarity descriptions in Appendix C characterize existing datasets, while the added analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated competitors remain TimeVAE, TimeVQVAE, RTSGAN, SDEGAN and LS4. COSCI-GAN is newly discussed and cited but does not participate in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds a reported forecasting evaluation across k=3, 5 and 7, plus retained-variance and filtering-diagnostic measurements. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, training budgets, metrics and selected dataset-specific embedding dimensions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables D.1, D.2 and D.7 substantially expand component analysis: variance retained by ICA/FPC, missing-value and filtering failures, and embedding-size sensitivity of downstream forecasting. Earlier similarity, runtime and LLM-backbone ablations are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: New Table D.2 explicitly reports filtering statistics averaged across five seeds. This adds repeated-run information for that analysis; it does not establish increased repetition of the retained benchmarks, whose uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and all matched earlier appendix tables retain their numerical results. v2 adds substantial evidence about representation loss, generation failures and forecasting sensitivity. For example, Table D.2 reports missing-value rates of 3.87%, 36.29% and 58.82% for ICA at k=3, 5 and 7; Table D.7 reports corresponding synthetic-only traffic RMSEs of 0.730, 0.655 and 0.790.

T1.justification: The textual encoder/inference definitions, embedding and reconstruction equations, norm-filtering derivation and diversity-based stopping criterion are unchanged. Added examples and empirical variance measurements introduce no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of efficient LLM-based generation from compact embeddings, competitive fidelity and forecasting utility, and support for textual conditioning. The additions support or discuss these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets larger embeddings as producing more incomplete generations and discusses the filtering diagnostics. It also expands limitations and future directions concerning linear embeddings, full fine-tuning and forecasting-focused utility evaluation. Much of the expanded ICA explanation already appeared in v1 Appendix A.2.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future code release with a reported release and repository location. v2 explicitly identifies full LLM fine-tuning and adds worked duplicate/missing-value examples in Appendix A.3, clarifying implementation without demonstrating a procedural change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a paragraph on specialized generation architectures and a new COSCI-GAN citation to Seyfi et al. (2022). It reinforces the existing positioning around pretrained-model reuse; the other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Localized expansions affect related work, result interpretation, filtering explanations and the conclusion, whose short limitations paragraph becomes a structured future-work discussion. The overall section structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Three appendix tables are added, existing tables are relocated and renumbered, and the author block is reformatted. Main Tables 1–2 now share a page. Figures 1, 2 and A.1 and the retained tables preserve their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The new diagnostics, forecasting ablation and code-access information improve transparency and support for design choices while preserving the original comparisons. The gain is limited by interpretation: Section 5.3 describes an overall discard rate below 2%, although Table D.2 separately reports missing-value rates up to 58.82% and Appendix A.3 says these samples are discarded. The added evidence is useful, but this distinction needs clearer explanation.
